articles.title: The root-to-tip revolution! An A-Z of how to eat plants in full – for extra flavour, fibre and savings
articles.summary: If you discard the peels, skins, stalks and seeds when consuming fruit and vegetables you are missing out on a lot of value. Here’s what to incorporate into your diet – and what to avoid. Do you peel your potatoes, deseed your squash and core your cauliflower?
body: The tough ends of asparagus are traditionally discarded, but they have plenty of flavour. The chef Tom Hunt, who writes the Guardian’s Waste not column, suggests freezing them until you have enough to make soup (you’ll need to blend and ideally sieve it); or blanching them and whizzing them into a salad dressing or flavoured butter.

Why go to such effort? “Leftovers are a valuable source of fibre and worth incorporating into meals, especially given that 96% of adults do not meet the recommended daily intake of 30g of fibre,” says Sammie Gill, a senior nutrition scientist at the British Nutrition Foundation. But fibre is not the only benefit. “Peels, stalks and seeds are also a rich source of plant chemicals, such as polyphenols. Studies show that different polyphenols are linked with different health effects, from brain health to metabolic health.”

articles.title: I spent months testing pillows to find six top picks for every kind of sleeper
articles.summary: If your pillows are flatter than a pancake, it’s time to upgrade. From foam and latex to classic down, there is one here that’s right for you. Could these three pillows unseat my favorite? Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I t’s pretty common advice that you should invest in anything that connects you to the ground. Most people think of shoes, tires and mattresses. However, I think people overlook things such as socks and pillows. The humble pillow can spell the difference between a fantastic night’s sleep and tossing and turning until dawn.
Goldilocks and I are on the same page. You need a pillow that isn’t too soft, hard, cold or hot. It needs to be just right.

I have been testing and reviewing products for more than 13 years, including for the Guardian’s Filter US since October 2025, with items such as bath towels, dryer balls and space heaters. I got my start at a product-testing lab where I tested household products under a combination of established and bespoke standards, and I specialized in washing machines and fabric care, and helped develop sleep lab protocols. I’m all about making sure products live up to what is advertised on the tin and provide good value. Plus, I love naps.

A good pillow should be able to provide support without feeling hard and be soft without completely enveloping you. To test this, I placed a 20lb weight on each pillow’s center and measured the amount of compression.

articles.title: Pilots Kept Contact With Controllers During Nationwide Halt to Flights
articles.summary: Pilots were generally able to maintain contact with air traffic controllers and airline staff on the ground despite an outage that caused a nearly five-hour halt to departures.
body: Pilots were able to maintain communications with air traffic controllers and airline dispatchers during the nationwide halt to most departing flights imposed by federal officials for nearly five hours on Friday.

A representative of the union that represents about 17,000 pilots at American Airlines said on Monday that it had received no reports of crews losing radio contact with controllers. Some pilots noticed radio static, but that isn’t uncommon, said Dennis Tajer, a spokesman for the union, the Allied Pilots Association.
Even so, the union said it supported the hourslong ground stop called by the Federal Aviation Administration, a part of the Department of Transportation.
Southwest Airlines dispatchers, who help to plan and guide the carrier’s flights, also reported no disruption of direct communications or data before the ground stop was ordered.
points: Pilots were generally able to maintain contact with air traffic controllers and airline staff on the ground despite an outage that caused a nearly five-hour halt to departures.

articles.title: An Intriguing Approach to Slow Alzheimer’s Shows Mixed Results
articles.summary: The device, a headset delivering light and sound, is based on the theory that audiovisual stimulation can evoke brainwave responses that might help preserve neurological function.
body: The largest trial to date of a headset device that delivers flickering light and sound in an attempt to slow the progression of Alzheimer’s has delivered mixed results.

Results of the study of the device, presented on Monday evening at a major Alzheimer’s conference, showed that the 12-month trial involving participants with mild to moderate Alzheimer’s did not achieve its primary goal. The overall group of patients who used the audiovisual device did not experience slower cognitive decline than those who used an inactive placebo device called a sham.

Patients with moderate Alzheimer’s showed no benefit at all from the system, called Spectris, according to data provided by the company, Cognito Therapeutics, which sponsored the trial. But for patients with mild Alzheimer’s, data generally suggested they could experience slower decline with the device, particularly if they used it nearly every day for close to the recommended 60 minutes.
Based on that, Cognito’s chief executive, Christian Howell, said the company planned to seek Food and Drug Administration approval.

articles.title: Naming your feelings can be harder than you think. This simple tool can help
articles.summary: About 10% of people have significant trouble identifying their emotions – which makes it harder to know what to do about them. Naming emotions is a core skill that most people develop as children, and it might seem like second nature.
body: That’s why a simple tool called the feelings wheel has gained popularity in therapists’ offices and classrooms over recent years.

At first glance, it looks a little like a pie chart: three concentric circles sliced into colored sections, with each region representing a different category of emotion. The innermost circle lists broad core feelings (sad/happy/angry), which split off into gradually more specific sub-emotions in the outer rings (remorseful/proud/humiliated).

Created by US psychologist Dr Gloria Willcox during the early 1980s, the feelings wheel is a tool designed to help people identify and clearly name their emotions, by moving gradually from broad blanket terms to more nuanced ones. The wheel has surged in popularity in recent years, thanks in part to its visual appeal – you can get it as a laminated office poster, as a wooden desk chart on a spin-stand or even stitched onto a cushion.

But do people really need this much help with the seemingly simple task of naming everyday feelings? Experts say that in many cases, the answer is yes – and behind this difficulty is an evidence-based scientific concept known as emotional granularity.

articles.title: Stella Cherfas obituary
articles.summary: My friend Stella Cherfas, who has died aged 101, helped popularise yoga in Britain through her classes that spanned several decades. She was a well-known fixture in many of London’s community spaces, notably teaching free weekly classes at Covent Garden Community Centre’s Seven Dials Club.
body: Her lifelong involvement with hatha yoga began in the 1950s when she attended classes led by Sir Paul Dukes, a former MI6 agent and author of Yoga for the Western World (1959), while living in Johannesburg. His approach united mind, body and spirit, but without pretentious mysticism. At the end of his course, he asked Stella to continue teaching the group.

Moving to London in the 60s, she began teaching hatha yoga using Dukes’s methods, while also ensuring it could be practised by anyone, regardless of age or physical limitation, and challenging the esoteric stereotypes of the day.

Born in Kraków, Poland, Stella was the daughter of Manek Rein, a solicitor, and Bronia (nee Infeld), first cousin to the physicist Leopold Infeld, who worked with Einstein. Rising antisemitism led the family to seek better opportunities elsewhere, and in 1935 they moved to South Africa. Several relatives were later to perish in Auschwitz.

articles.title: Hospitals Brace for Medicaid Work Rules and Deep Funding Cuts
articles.summary: Eskenazi Hospital in Indianapolis is dispatching teams into the city’s low-income neighborhoods to help educate patients on keeping their Medicaid coverage.
body: Hospitals across the country are mobilizing an expansive outreach effort in an attempt to ensure that roughly 19 million patients do not lose their insurance coverage under new Medicaid work rules that begin in January.

Saying the requirements are generating widespread anxiety and confusion, health care executives are using a variety of methods to help guide the Americans who will be affected. They are deploying staff and volunteers to contact patients with text messages, phone calls and offers of help.

The rules dictate that able-bodied adults without young children either work, volunteer or attend school or job training for at least 80 hours a month. Republicans included the rules last year as part of President Trump’s package of tax cuts and reductions in safety net spending, including nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts.
Hospitals and other health centers are detailing what evidence people in many cases must provide — pay stubs or other proof of work or school attendance — to maintain coverage.

articles.title: John H. Powers III to Lead NIAID Amid Turmoil
articles.summary: Dr. John H. Powers III was appointed director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, a powerful post held for decades by Dr. Anthony Fauci.
body: Dr. John H. Powers III, an infectious disease researcher, was appointed on Monday to lead the National Institutes of Health division on infectious diseases, giving him control of a politically contentious institute with a budget of over $6.5 billion and responsibility for research into such pressing threats as measles and Ebola.

His designation as director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, a position held for nearly four decades by Dr. Anthony S. Fauci, caps a rapid rise for Dr. Powers, who until recently was an N.I.H. contractor and clinical trials design specialist.

Since the start of the second Trump administration, Dr. Powers gained influence among senior health officials as he was tapped to study vaccine injuries, a priority of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

Early last year, Dr. Powers worked with Dr. Matthew Memoli, the No. 2 official at the N.I.H. and a critic of Covid vaccine mandates, to obtain sets of data related to vaccines and autism from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, according to emails reviewed by The New York Times.

articles.title: Where Chef Esther Choi Eats on Her Day Off in NYC
articles.summary: Celebrity chef and cookbook author Esther Choi, the chef behind Korean restaurants like mǒkbar and Ms. Yoo, shows us the cafe, bakery, and restaurants she visits weekly for everything from taro-mochi doughnuts to soup dumplings.
body: Choi starts her day with co-fermented coffee at Tera Espresso Bar, where all the beans are roasted in-house and signatures are co-fermented with fruits. She grabs her coffee made with beans that were fermented with tangerines and heads to pastry chef Dominique Ansel’s bakery, Papa D’Amour. Ansel shows her how he makes his labor-intensive taro-mochi doughnut that is filled with a strawberry jam and frozen before being fried up. Next is the viral butter-dipped vanilla soft serve that Choi gets to dip in the warm butter herself.

Choi then heads to NYC icon Pastis for lunch, ordering the cheese-crusted French onion soup, fries, and a dirty martini. The deeply flavorful French onion soup takes four hours to make. Choi recommends ordering your own — this is not a dish you’ll want to share. Her super briny vodka martini hits the table as Choi reminisces about working at Food Network nearby and coming to Pastis with co-workers.

articles.title: A Quick and Dirty History of Honey Traps, From Mata Hari to Mozhno Girls
articles.summary: While the term “honey trap” may call to mind KGB agent Elizabeth Jennings entrancing CIA assets on “The Americans,” the real phenomenon has deep historical roots.
body: Ever since Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with Chinese intelligence asset Alice Huang became public, the term has been everywhere, calling to mind KGB sleeper agent Elizabeth Jennings (and her wide variety of wigs) on The Americans, Ingrid Bergman fraternizing with Nazi collaborators in Notorious, and Eva Marie Saint’s slick Eve Kendall in North by Northwest. (Espionage fiction author John le Carré is widely credited with coining the phrase “honey trap” in his 1974 novel Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy, later defining it for the BBC as when you “put a girl in a chap’s way. It’s a sexual enticement operation.”) But the real-life phenomenon has far deeper and more interesting roots.

articles.title: Are US Flight Schedules Returning to Normal? What Thanksgiving Travelers Need to Know
articles.summary: The FAA issued a ground stop just days before the Thanksgiving travel rush, raising questions about whether flight schedules will return to normal in time for the holiday.
body: Travel chaos erupted at US airports over the weekend following a historic FAA ground stop that paused all flight takeoffs across the country for nearly five hours.

The ground stop, declared by the FAA amid air traffic control issues on Friday, November 13, stranded millions of fliers nationwide, with tens of thousands of flight delays and cancellations continuing for days. Now, with the busy Thanksgiving travel period fast approaching, travelers are wondering when US air travel system will return to normal.

Fortunately for travelers, both federal officials and airlines are doing everything they can to get flight schedules back on track and have airport operations running smoothly in time for the holiday rush. “Recovery to normal operations will be slow and steady,” says a November 15 statement from the FAA. “We ask for your patience as airlines work to get you to your destination.”

articles.title: The National Black Theatre Raised a Glass—and $1 Million—at Its Inaugural Fall Fête
articles.summary: The night celebrated historic achievements, reflection, and legacy while honoring esteemed creatives, including John Legend, Mike Jackson, Nona Hendryx, Sanford Biggers, and Margaret Anadu.
body: “Ordinary People” might be the title of a Grammy-winning song by John Legend. Yet Legend’s persona and career trajectory have proven to be anything but ordinary—as exemplified by his attendance and performance at The National Black Theatre’s inaugural Fall Fête.

The benefit gala recently welcomed Legend alongside Mickalene Thomas, Lena Waithe, Mike Jackson, Cyndi Lauper, and Donna Murphy to Current—a private event space within Pier 59 at Chelsea Piers. Inside the venue, a crowd gathered for a cocktail reception as the Kotchegna Dance Company helped kick off the evening with their powerful rhythmic processional while Reverend Rhonda Akanaké McLean-Nur poured libations to set the tone.

articles.title: How a New Restaurant Injected Retro “Latin Soul” Into a New-Build Space
articles.summary: This excerpt was originally published in Pre Shift, our newsletter for the hospitality industry. Subscribe for more first-person accounts, advice, and interviews. Opened at the end of October, Bar Nuestro is Washington, D.C.’s newest bistro serving European- and Latin-inspired dishes and drinks.
body: Daniella Senior: We wanted the space to really feel—even though it’s a new buildout—that it’s been there a long time. I’m kind of tired of the same aesthetic going around, one that’s almost too clean, too new, too matchy-matchy. I think that doesn’t, at times, help you communicate what the food is trying to communicate. For us, the food and the space work together. We wanted it to feel very Old World. We took a lot of inspiration from Vienna’s old corner cafes, which have been institutions for a while. We wanted a “We’ve been here a minute” type of feel.

From our furniture to our tiles, [the Bar Nuestro team and designer Shawn Hausman] sourced a lot of vintage pieces, about 25 percent of the furniture. We have chairs that came from Austria and Italy in the ’30s and fabric with vintage patterns. When Shawn was traveling through Europe, he’d send pictures of things he found, and I sourced accent pieces—like the credenza in our garden room, vases, menu holders, a vintage phone—in local vintage shops.
